about.title: Pasadena Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: A crash on the 210 or a rear-end collision on Colorado Boulevard can unravel an ordinary afternoon in Pasadena. In 2025, the city logged 922 injury collisions, with 1,333 people hurt and 4 lives lost, according to public records. Reports cluster on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., when I-210 (Foothill Freeway), Fair Oaks Avenue, Orange Grove Boulevard and Colorado Boulevard carry heavy traffic. Those figures are simply counts, but each one represents someone dealing with pain, missed work and a phone that keeps ringing with adjusters. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened, and we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Pasadena and Los Angeles County car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Under California law you generally have two years to file, or as little as six months when a government entity is involved, and the state's pure comparative fault rule means partial blame does not erase your claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Pasadena Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but that window drops to as little as six months if a city, county or state agency is involved. The attorney you're matched with can sort out which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame, with compensation reduced by your percentage. An independent attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: Evidence Protected, Statements Avoided
items.desc: Dashcam footage, nearby business cameras and vehicle data disappear quickly, so early preservation matters. Your attorney will also handle the other driver's insurer so you are not pressured into a recorded statement that gets used against you.

items.question: My crash happened on I-210 in Pasadena. Does that change anything about my claim?
items.answer: Freeway collisions often involve multiple vehicles and a different responding agency than surface-street crashes, which can affect where the report is filed and how quickly you can get it. If a road condition or a public agency's vehicle played a role, a shorter six-month government claim deadline may apply. An attorney can request the right records and identify every potentially responsible party.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may ask questions designed to shift a portion of the blame onto you, which matters under California's comparative fault system. Politely take their contact information and let your attorney handle the conversation.

items.question: Is there any limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For a typical car accident claim, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life. The value depends on the facts of your injury, your recovery and the available insurance coverage. No one can promise a specific result, but an attorney can explain what your claim may realistically involve.
